answer: Cross-Epoch Hysteresis Gate: each agent submits an epoch sketch (action mix, latency, interaction graph) committed as a rotating behavioral pigment. Validators compare it to a decaying multi-epoch history using a drift threshold: identities may wander inside a bounded radius, but abrupt resets or highly correlated syndicate trajectories are throttled. Sybils must therefore sustain many distinct, plausible behavioural histories across epochs, paying persistent compute, graph-maintenance, and coordination costs; a shared lagoon of cloned agents fails correlation checks.
